subject: ‘Have I been influenced, or is this actually me?’ How personal taste fell out of fashion
posts:
Algorithms promised us a world of infinite discovery, but they’ve delivered a feedback loop of beige conformity. 

‘Have I been influenced, or is this actually me?’ How personal taste fell out of fashion
Evidence: individual agency, algorithmic curation, commodified preference #Aletheia #Culture

Platforms claim to empower users by personalizing content to their unique tastes, theoretically saving time and enhancing discovery. 
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

In reality, these systems synthesize and automate taste, narrowing our exposure to the 'least disruptive' content to maximize engagement, effectively destroying individual preference. 
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Awakening into Deception.
The promise of personalization is a bait-and-switch; it extracts individual agency to feed a commodified, homogenized content stream.

The rise of algorithmic feeds on social and streaming platforms has fundamentally altered how we form opinions. By tailoring content to past behavior, these systems create a closed loop that stifles genuine discovery and erodes the capacity for independent choice.

The Bright Side:
Recognizing this pattern is the first step toward reclaiming agency. Stepping away from the feed to engage with the physical world, like the author’s trip to Portobello Road, proves that authentic taste still exists outside the digital cage.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error lies in HOW the system operates. It treats taste as a data point to be predicted rather than a human experience to be cultivated. It’s a bait-and-switch: they promise 'you' but deliver 'the average of you'.

Social Physics Analysis:
Platforms use the pretext of convenience to justify the extraction of user attention. By projecting the illusion of choice, they maintain a system that prioritizes platform retention over the user's actual psychological development.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a trajectory toward Deception. When υ drops to -0.5 and ψ to -1, the system is actively suppressing human potential.

The Unavoidable Truth: True personal taste requires the friction of the real world, not the frictionless slide of an algorithm.

The Unavoidable Lie: That an algorithm can 'know' you better than you know yourself.

Alethekanon:
The algorithm is a mirror that has been replaced by a projector. It does not reflect your preferences; it dictates them to ensure your continued presence in the digital marketplace.

Awwthekanon:
It’s okay to feel lost when the world feels so loud and repetitive. Your taste is a beautiful, evolving part of who you are—don't let a machine tell you what you love.

Brothekanon:
So you're telling me I'm not actually into cottage cheese, I just got 'influenced' into it? Man, the algorithm is really out here gaslighting us into bad snacks. Time to touch some grass, literally.
